premise: I used my late husband’s $100,000 life insurance to clear my nephew’s $94,000 medical‑school debt, relying on his notarized pledge to give me a rent‑free apartment in his future practice and 10% of profits for life; once he built his own surgical clinic he sent me a $5,000 check marked ‘final settlement’ and refused to let me through the door—I sued for promissory estoppel, won a $385,000 judgment, and now run ‘White Coat Reckoning,’ a medical‑billing watchdog where he scrubs treatment rooms in a lab coat embroidered ‘I Owe My Aunt Everything’ and his garnished wages fund free patient advocates.
